decisions.reason: The same source message already fully establishes the sensor-board orientation, top-edge connector placement, interboard alignment, and short straight cable routing in this Requirement.
The source adds mechanical placement and alignment constraints but does not change the established connector types, pinouts, or electrical interboard topology.
The source concerns connectors on the main and sensor boards, not the battery connector on the power board.
The stated rail orientation and connector-placement rules apply specifically to the main and sensor boards and do not alter the power-board layout.
Mechanical connector alignment does not change the monitored rails, monitoring IC, channel allocation, or measurement coverage.
Short straight cable routing is a mechanical consequence of connector alignment and does not replace the existing cable-length, pull-up, bus-speed, or series-resistor requirements.
The source does not change standalone regulator capacity, source selection, activation conditions, or powered loads.
The panel power-button connector is a two-pin control connector, and the source does not change its board assignment, electrical connection, or behavior.
The source does not alter the BOOT control, reset connection, or associated capacitance values.
The mechanical connector-placement decision does not change the specified ESP32 module.
The source does not change the USB-C programming interface or native USB behavior.

The source changes physical placement of sensor-board connectors but does not change their inventory, types, pinouts, connected modules, or count; those placement constraints are already represented by the sensor-board mechanical Requirement.
